strongest_angle: The 2021 Meltwater Champions Chess Tour Finals featured a critical endgame blunder where Teimour Radjabov, under extreme time pressure, failed to find the only drawing move against Hikaru Nakamura.

key_facts.fact: During the 2021 Meltwater Champions Chess Tour Finals, Teimour Radjabov had only six seconds to decide his 48th move against Hikaru Nakamura.
In the game, Teimour Radjabov played 48 Kd2, which allowed Hikaru Nakamura to play 48... Ke5, securing a winning position for Black.
Following the move 49 Kd3, Hikaru Nakamura played 49... Kd5, forcing Teimour Radjabov to resign due to zugzwang.
The game between Teimour Radjabov and Hikaru Nakamura occurred during the 2021 Meltwater Champions Chess Tour Finals, where Radjabov ultimately finished in second place.

quotes.text: Six seconds! That’s how long Radjabov had to choose his next move in the diagram below, from an online rapid game in 2021. Plausible options are 1 Kd3, 1 Kd2 and 1 Kc3, but two of these lose by force.
